scope: slice 2: timeline gestures to v2 intents on the ordinary Show editor route
invariants: One adopted gesture is one owner intent, one candidate, one history entry and one provider save; the adapter decides no edit semantics and writes no record.

Identity is allocated only at submission and only for a gesture that can change the record; an unknown Clip, a Group Clip use, an out-of-bounds split time or a destination outside Show End refuses with the allocator untouched.
A rigid connected move is the temporal owner's traversal: the adapter emits one move and shifts no neighbour, and drop feedback clamps and collides on the whole component.
Duplication is linked: the copy consumes the source effective Pattern instance and no gesture mints a runtime.
Cut is exact adjacency: snapping and collision are pixel affordances, the submitted times are whole milliseconds, and a one-millisecond gap draws no junction.
A refusal or no-op leaves the record identity, history, timestamp and provider untouched, and surfaces the owner's message in the existing pilot status vocabulary.
The v1 route is unchanged: the v2 surface consumes only the version-agnostic view model and never the v1 projections or store mutators.
partitions: gesture kind: drag move, cross-Layer re-placement, trailing resize, leading resize, split, linked duplicate, delete
direction: grow versus shrink on each edge; earlier versus later on a move; unmoved edge and unmoved drop as no-ops
topology: Clip with no Transition, Clip inside a Crossfade chain, whole-output carrier with a Property ramp, Group Clip use
leading resize outcome: narrowed window versus window closed to zero, with and without a carrier ramp
drop feedback: free drop, boundary-snapped drop, Alt raw-millisecond drop, component clamp at zero and at Show End, colliding drop
input: pointer drag, pointer edge drag, double-click split, keyboard nudge and edge step, S/D/Delete, Escape cancel, busy guard
admission: applied, owner refusal, adapter refusal before admission, Undo, Redo
DELETE-READD placement: replacement at exact adjacency versus one millisecond later
sequences: drag move -> keyboard move -> trailing resize -> leading resize -> split -> collided duplicate refusal -> duplicate -> delete -> Undo -> Redo -> provider readback
fresh two-Clip v2 Show -> delete the second Clip -> add a replacement at the boundary + 1 ms (gap) -> delete it -> add a replacement at the exact boundary (derived Cut)
gesture on a Clip inside a Crossfade chain -> both members translate by one delta with the Transition duration preserved
leading edge dragged onto its outgoing neighbour with a ramp carrier -> Reset consumes complete projections
oracles: The record saved through the closed admission deep-equals the record the pilot's typed intent produces for the same parameters, plus an independently stated per-Clip interval and Transition duration for every temporal case.
Store state after each gesture: one provider write, one history entry holding the exact preimage, and the preimage object itself unmutated.
Undo and Redo restore the exact prior and edited records through undoShowV2Pilot / redoShowV2Pilot.
The view model projected from the saved record: a derived-cut junction with a null transitionId only at exact adjacency, and no Transition resurrected by a replacement Clip.
The rendered surface: aria-labels naming each Clip's interval, drop-preview collision state, focus after a created Clip, and the status line.

The real authenticated route at 1440 and 390 px: gesture outcomes read back from the drawn labels and from GET /api/shows?show-version=2, Fast and Precise Stage capture sequences, zero console errors, zero overflow.

Group Clip uses, Markers, the Layout lane and property lanes stay inert on the v2 surface.
